title: Amazon Projects Negative Free Cash Flow From $220B AI Spend
summary:
Prasad Kalyanaraman, AWS vice president of infrastructure, cautioned that the current pace of cloud buildout may create internal budget pressures for at least two years. This financial shift stems from a $220 billion investment program for artificial intelligence that has already pushed the company's overall free cash flow into negative territory, according to internal communications and AWS CFO John Felton. Internal emails show Amazon projected $5 billion in Nvidia GB300 rack deliveries in August, followed by monthly shipments of approximately $3 billion.

The scale of the buildout has caused bottlenecks at some AWS data centers, which possess the physical space for new hardware but lack the power required to activate it. To secure its supply chain, Amazon is taking ownership of equipment early and storing the units in warehouses, which ties up capital before the racks can be deployed.

🚨HOLY. Business Insider obtained internal Amazon emails projecting $5 BILLION in Nvidia GB300 racks deliveries in August, then roughly $3 BILLION EVERY MONTH.

Some AWS data centers have room for the racks but NOT enough power to turn them on. Equipment is being staged in warehouses, while Amazon takes ownership earlier, tying up cash before deployment.

At an internal September staff meeting, AWS CFO John Felton joked to infrastructure chief Prasad Kalyanaraman: "You've taken us free cash flow negative as a company, so congratulations."

AWS's infrastructure chief expects Amazon's free cash flow to remain negative for 'the next couple of years or so.'
